text:
sam_support: Customer hit intermittent JSON.parse failures when using structured_output in streaming mode. Root errors: 'Unexpected end of JSON input' and 'Invalid escape sequence'. Logs attached.

klara_customer: Repro steps: call Redwood API with prompt containing Windows path 'C:\Users\klara\docs\report.json' using stream:true and structured mode. Client does JSON.parse on assembled chunks and fails ~10% of runs.

klara_customer: Example of assembled stream (sanitized):
>>> {"document":{"path":"C:\Users\klara\docs\report.json","title":"Q1 report"}}
But sometimes we see double-escaped path: 
>>> {"document":{"path":"C:\\Users\\klara\\docs\\report.json","title":"Q1 report"}}
And other runs end with a truncated object: 
>>> {"document":{"path":"C:\Users\klara\docs\report.json","title":"Q1 report"
... (no trailing brace)
We also observed a literal CR () byte appearing before the closing quote in one chunk which made the JSON parser bail.

maria_engineer: Can you paste the client code? Are you concatenating chunks as UTF-8 strings or doing any manual escaping?

klara_customer: Node fetch streaming snippet:
```js
const res = await fetch(apiUrl, {method:'POST', body:payload});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let text = '';
while(true){
  const {value, done} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  text += new TextDecoder().decode(value);
  try { JSON.parse(text); break }
  catch(e) { /* keep reading */ }
}
```

maria_engineer: That parsing-on-partial approach is brittle. Two likely contributing factors: (1) chunk boundary splitting an escape sequence (chunk ends with a single backslash) so after concatenation the escape becomes invalid, (2) multibyte characters (emoji) split across chunks causing decoder to insert replacement chars or shift bytes. Did you have emoji in any fields?

klara_customer: Yes — titles include an emoji '📝'. One of the failing runs showed 'Invalid token 	' from JSON.parse.

maria_engineer: Quick repro we ran locally that reproduces the failure ~20% of the time:
1) Prompt that includes a Windows path like `C:\a\b\c` and a title with an emoji.
2) stream:true & structured_mode:true
3) capture binary chunks and force a split at a random byte boundary (simulate network chunking).
4) assemble using naive TextDecoder + string concat and JSON.parse.

We saw three variants: properly escaped path, double-escaped path (extra backslashes introduced across chunk boundary), and truncated/malformed JSON (missing trailing brace).

jordan_infra: Also check the client's TextDecoder call — if a multibyte sequence is split, TextDecoder may emit a replacement character unless you use the streaming mode (`new TextDecoder().decode(value, {stream:true})`) which preserves incomplete sequences. That plus a backslash at a boundary explains why escapes get corrupted.

maria_engineer: Short-term mitigations:
- On client: stop calling JSON.parse on partial text; buffer until you get a complete top-level JSON object (count braces or wait for a final event).
- Use TextDecoder with {stream:true} when decoding raw chunks.
- If possible, switch to SSE or framed JSON events so each message is atomic.

We also have a feature-flag 'atomic_json_stream' that packages complete JSON objects into single events for streaming clients — we can enable it for affected accounts while we harden runtime.

klara_customer: Can you enable it for acct_9876? We can't change the client quickly.

sam_support: File a support escalation and enable the feature-flag. I'll loop in the account team.

infra-bot: feature-flag 'atomic_json_stream' enabled for account acct_9876 by @sam_support

maria_engineer: Follow-ups: we've added a unit test that injects random chunk splits and emoji + Windows paths into our streaming runtime. PR incoming that improves streaming escape handling and uses an escape-inspector to avoid leaving a dangling backslash at chunk boundaries.

sam_support: Thanks everyone — klara, please confirm after you try SSE or the flag. I'll keep the ticket open. :pray:
